features.label: Features and capabilities
features.tagline: Digital time clock, time tracking, roster, issues and tasks in one platform.
features.highlight: People clock in, look at their roster, carry out tasks and report a problem from their phone. There is no app to install.
features.intro: WinProx is an online platform an organisation uses to keep people, working hours, rosters, locations and day-to-day work. It is used for time tracking, staff planning, visits at customers, maintenance, inspection rounds and following up issues. Depending on the plan, RSZ/CIAO reporting, GPS work visits, sensors, ESG measurements and software links are also available. Everything works in the browser: administrators usually on a computer, people on a smartphone, via a QR code or on a clock screen.
features.source: This page describes the features, what is available, and the main conditions.
features.footer_right: See also: Technical fact sheet for hosting, privacy and security, and API & Webhooks for software links.

full.title: WinProx Time
full.body: WinProx Time is the digital time clock, together with time tracking, the roster and day-to-day follow-up.
items: Clock in and out, and see who is present.
Set the recorded hours next to the roster.
Plan shifts and publish them.
Handle leave and time-off requests.
Manage issues, tasks and inspection rounds.
Manage locations, teams, people and units.
RSZ/CIAO presence reporting can be turned on in settings. Optional GPS work visits tie a visit to a location.

full.title: Checkmate
full.body: Checkmate is the plan for people who work at customer sites, for example in construction or cleaning. A visit starts only when GPS is within the set distance of the customer location.
items: Clocking in and out can be done from the Clock Point icon. Presence, the timesheet and My hours are included.
You manage customers and their locations under Customers and Locations. A location can have a unit for the whole site.
You import customers in bulk from CSV or Excel, with location details on each row.
For each customer you see the month: visits, time worked and hours per location. Export that as CSV or print it.
RSZ/CIAO reporting is on from the start, once the CBE number is in settings. You pass the hours to the social secretariat. WinProx does not file Dimona and does not calculate pay.
The price is €5 per active worker per month. You set the number of licences yourself.
New organisations can start with a trial month of 25 licences, a demo team, a worker and demo customers. During the trial there are no limits on units or documents.
Checkmate has its own short manual, instead of the general WinProx manual.

full.title: Corporate
full.body: Corporate is for organisations that want to extend WinProx with links, sensors and measurements. That sits apart from ordinary time tracking and the roster.
items: API and webhooks to exchange data with other software.
IoT Connect for events from connected sensors.
ESG and compliance tools for measurements, indicators and follow-up tasks.

full.title: Time clock and hours
full.body: WinProx records when someone starts and stops. Administrators follow presence and set the hours next to the planned shifts.
items: People clock in and out with the Clock Point QR code. On a fixed clock, each punch scans the code on the sticker or on the clock screen. The home-screen icon and the sign-in link do not clock in by themselves. On Checkmate, a worker can clock in and out from the icon.
A photo of the sticker can also be used away from the door. The QR code on the clock screen changes by itself and expires, so an old photo no longer works.
You see who is present and the timesheet, and each person sees only their own shifts under My hours.
WinProx compares planned and recorded time with a margin of 15 minutes. A mark opens that person’s hours for that day straight away.
If someone forgot to clock in, an administrator can add the record by hand.

If someone clocks in during leave, time off, a public holiday or sickness, that becomes a point of attention: a warning next to that person on the presence list, and a red clock-in block with a message on the phone. It is a signal to check the record, not a judgement on working time.

You turn on RSZ/CIAO reporting in settings. The link with the social security office is confirmed before sending starts. You pass the hours to the social secretariat. WinProx does not file Dimona and does not calculate pay.

full.title: Clock Point
full.body: Clock Point is where people open their work tools, in the browser. After clock-in, a welcome screen can show the day’s round as a timeline.
items: Clock in and out, see the published roster, see one’s own hours, request leave or time off.
Carry out tasks, follow an inspection round, and start a work visit when GPS is on.
An optional clock screen shows a QR code that changes by itself. You pair the screen with a one-time code and a confirmation.
You choose when the screen is on, for example from 06:00 to 19:00. Outside those hours it can stay off, or show a rest screen: photos, a clock face or a flip clock.

Without a smartphone: tap the screen, find the first name by letters; on an open shift choose break or clock-out, then enter a personal four-digit PIN. Someone without a PIN chooses one on the spot, twice.
After two wrong attempts, that worker is blocked for one minute.

full.title: Roster
full.body: An administrator plans shifts in Time → Roster and publishes them. Published shifts appear on Clock Point.
items: Choose a team or a location first. Without that choice the roster does not load.
Week or month view. Several shifts on one day, as a code or as a free block, for example 07:00–15:00. A note per shift is possible, and so is a group or unit on the shift.
You copy a week to at most 26 weeks in a row. WinProx skips days that already have shifts or absences. Notes are not copied.
WinProx asks you to save unsaved changes first if you leave the page or switch week or month.
Find a replacement: WinProx suggests available colleagues. The original block becomes an absence and the replacement gets the same time slot.

Leave, time off and sickness can be a whole day or part of a day. Those blocks do not count as hours worked. You set the shift types under Time → Shift types. Public holidays and replacement days live under Time → Public holidays.
Public holidays and replacement days have their own colour. A fixed day off is grey and can still be filled in.

The default week target is 38 hours, adjustable per worker. Targets and differences take the work pattern and public holidays into account. Without a reliable target the figure stays empty. It is a count for the overview, not a judgement on working time.
Per location you set a minimum staffing level: how many people are needed per shift type. WinProx shows where the planned staffing falls short. A shortfall does not block saving or publishing.
Restore points of roster changes are kept for 30 days. The list shows at most 40. You see date, time, source, people and days, and what disappears, comes back or changes.

A locked day, a shift that has since moved to another day, or approved leave can block a restore. If the roster differs or a request is still open, WinProx asks for a confirmation. That confirmation covers only the difference you see. If the roster has changed in the meantime, WinProx restores nothing and shows the new difference. A successful restore can itself be undone.
On Clock Point, people see only their own published shifts for that month. After a publication or a later change, a mark appears.
A team roster is optional. People then see colleagues’ published week shifts at their own location. Absences are shown in a neutral way.
The planning feature can be switched off. Existing shifts stay stored. The clock, QR sign-in and tasks remain available.
Print opens the visible period on landscape A4.

full.title: Leave and time off
full.body: People request leave or time off on Clock Point. An administrator decides in Time → Requests. This request is not for reporting sickness, and no email is sent.
items: A request runs from a start date to an end date, at most 31 days, and not in the past.
A refusal needs a reason. After the decision you can see who approved or refused.
An open or approved request can be withdrawn as long as the absence has not started.
On approval, the existing shifts stay at first. WinProx then replaces them in the roster with the absence.

full.title: Issues
full.body: WinProx helps to report a problem at a location, assign it and follow it up.
items: You create an issue from the QR code on a unit, from the back office, or from a connected sensor when IoT is set up.
Administrators can filter and approve QR issues. On the public QR page an issue appears only after approval.
For anonymous issues, contact details or an email confirmation can be asked. Once the reporter uses the link, the issue can be marked as confirmed.
Recurring maintenance can be paused or closed.

full.title: Tasks
full.body: One issue can have several tasks. Each task goes to one team, and optionally to one worker in that team.
items: For each task you set priority, deadline and notes.
Follow-up runs through the task list or a QR code on the floor.
An administrator can always change or clear the assigned worker, for example when someone is ill.

full.title: Finishing tasks
full.body: People finish the tasks assigned to them. When everything is done, an administrator closes the issue.
items: When finishing, they can add a note and a photo.
The administrator sees the status and the history.
Workers use the unit QR code, or Clock Point with an open GPS work visit.

full.title: Dashboard
full.body: The dashboard is the start of the day. At the top is the question What do you want to do?, with shortcuts to the main tools.
items: Roster and presence, a new day task or inspection round, locations and workers.
New issues and open tasks. With Time: who is present now.
A warning when someone clocks in during leave, time off, a public holiday or sickness. Open leave and time-off requests.
New workers a team leader just created, until an administrator saves or deactivates them. Briefings and reports. New organisations choose a starting setup here.

full.title: Organisation, locations and people
full.body: Administrators set up the organisation with locations, teams, people and units. A unit can be a room, a vehicle, a machine or another asset. Each location can also have a unit for the whole site.
items: Manage categories and locations. Add units one by one or in bulk, including from CSV.
Find and manage workers under People → Workers. A portrait photo is optional.
Make documents and notices available on the portal. Set which sites a worker may use.
Floater teams can clock in at every location. Other workers only at the sites assigned to them.
Setting a team leader, or changing an icon, phone, PIN or passkey, is done via Edit.

full.title: QR portals
full.body: All QR portals open in the browser. There is no install from the App Store or Google Play.
items: A unit’s QR code opens what is switched on for that unit: create an issue, do a unit check, or record a measurement.
A unit page that was already loaded can stay usable without internet. Clocking in still needs a fresh scan.

full.title: Unit checks
full.body: A unit check is a quick check: is this unit in order, for example during a round.
items: From the QR code the person chooses OK or Not OK. With OK, no separate issue is needed.
Optional: a checklist, a remark and up to four photos.
The history is under Work → Unit checks.

full.title: Inspection rounds
full.body: An inspection round is a set route along units or locations. It can be one-off or recurring.
items: At each stop: all in order, a problem turned into an issue straight away, or skip with a reason.
A stop that stands for the whole location shows that location’s name.
With Time and GPS, today’s round appears under Where do I need to go. The round can be printed from the task.
An existing round can be marked as a favourite and copied. The copy takes the title and the stops and is one-off for today by default.

full.title: Measurements, photos and GPS
full.body: WinProx can keep simple measurements without the full ESG module. Photos belong with issues, tasks and checks. GPS on a mobile unit is not the same as the GPS check on a Checkmate visit.
items: Examples of measurements: mileage, temperature, or the status of a device. The fields live under Work → Unit measurements and you switch them on per category and per unit.
Measurements arrive via a QR code or the API. A measurement can reach other software through the webhook unit.measurement.recorded.

Up to four photos on an issue, a completion or a unit check. Per unit, up to four unit photos and one background photo. Photos are reduced on the device before upload. A reporter’s photos on the public portal become visible only after the issue is approved.
For mobile units, such as a vehicle or a machine, the location can be recorded. You switch that on per category. You open the history in the back office, and a point opens in Maps.

full.title: Calendar
full.body: The calendar shows tasks, issues and reservations by month, week and day.
items: From the calendar you print that day’s briefing.

full.title: Briefing
full.body: The briefing is a printable overview of the open tasks for a chosen day, by team.
items: You reach the briefing from the dashboard, the task list and the calendar.

full.title: Reports
full.body: On search and overview pages you export or print the filtered list.
items: CSV for Excel, for example, or print to PDF. The same filters as the list. At most 5,000 rows per export.
WinProx Time shows a timesheet. Customer statistics show time worked, visits and hours per work address and per month.

full.title: Reservations
full.body: WinProx can reserve a shared asset with a time slot, for example a meeting room or a vehicle.
items: An administrator turns reservations on for a category, and allows them per unit.
Guests book via the unit’s QR code. Confirmation is sent by email.

full.title: ESG and compliance
full.body: Corporate ESG tools are for organisations that want to collect and follow measurements on environment, safety and compliance. They sit on top of ordinary issues, tasks and unit measurements.
items: Define indicators, record measurements, and link follow-up tasks to a measurement.
Enter data via the portal, the back office or the API.

full.title: IoT Connect
full.body: IoT Connect lets connected sensors send an event to WinProx.
items: A sensor can send an alarm. WinProx turns that into an approved issue, with a task.
Measurements can also feed the ESG tools. For IoT Connect a separate gateway token is enough; a full API is not always required.

full.title: API and webhooks
full.body: The API and webhooks let other software exchange data with WinProx. An API fetches data or sends it in. A webhook sends a message on its own as soon as something happens.
items: You set tokens and outbound webhooks under Settings → API.
The technical detail is in the API & Webhooks sheet and the Technical fact sheet.

full.title: Look and QR stickers
full.body: The portal can be made recognisable for your own organisation.
items: In settings you set a logo, change the background and choose the colour of the buttons.
You print QR codes as a sticker sheet or on A6, A5 or A4. Avery and Herma sheets, among others, fit.

full.title: Work menu
full.body: Administrators choose which extra parts appear in the work menu.
items: Per organisation you can switch on: calendar, reservations, inspection rounds and unit measurements.
When a part is off, it is no longer reachable in the back office. Existing QR codes on units keep working.
Issues and tasks are the main switch. Turn that off, and the other work parts leave the menu as well.

full.title: Translations
full.body: After approval, WinProx can queue texts for translation.
items: Translation uses local AI. For this, the texts are not sent to an external AI cloud.
Translations are usually processed daily, without a fixed turnaround. Administrators can correct them themselves.

full.title: Roles and access
full.body: WinProx uses four roles in the same platform.
items: Administrator: the whole organisation, the settings and the subscription.
Staff member: day-to-day follow-up, without billing.
Worker: the work via Clock Point and the QR codes, without an ordinary back-office login.
Team leader: manage workers, release their icon, and take photos via Clock Point.
Administrators and staff sign in with email and password, or with Microsoft. The email address must belong to an existing WinProx account.
Workers use Clock Point with their name and icon. Other software connects with API keys, not with the ordinary login.

full.title: Subscription and limits
full.body: Each organisation has its own environment. The plan sets how many licences, units and documents are available. A licence counts for a colleague with a back-office login or for a worker. A colleague who also uses the clock counts as one licence.
items: The number of units is ten times the number of licences. The number of documents depends on the plan. Locations and photos are unlimited. Each location automatically gets a unit for the whole site.

full.title: No app needed
full.body: WinProx works in the browser. Administrators use a computer. People open Clock Point and the QR portals on their smartphone.
items: No install from the App Store or Google Play. Clock Point can sit as a shortcut on the phone’s home screen.

full.title: In short
full.body: WinProx brings time tracking, staff planning and day-to-day follow-up together in one online platform.
items: You use what fits the organisation: time clock, roster, customer visits, inspection rounds and maintenance.
Checkmate is for work visits at customers, with RSZ/CIAO reporting. Corporate adds API links, sensors and ESG follow-up.
WinProx works in the browser. A separate app is not needed.

technical.label: Technical fact sheet
technical.tagline: Hosting, privacy, availability and security for IT.
technical.intro: Overview for IT and security. Each customer organisation has its own separated environment. WinProx runs in the browser. An optional fixed clock display can stand on site.
technical.footer_left: WinProx · info@winprox.app · Product overview, not legal advice or an SLA.
technical.footer_right: Questions? We are happy to walk through the DPA, subprocessors and integrations.

full.title: Hosting
items: Production in the **EU**, at **Cloud86**, on Linux.
Access via **HTTPS** (encrypted connection).
Email via servers in the EU. Billing monthly via Stripe.
Pricing: **€59** (5 licences + 50 units), **€99** (10 + 100), **€199** (25 + 250), **€349** (50 + 500) per month. Corporate on request.

full.title: Backups
items: Automatic **daily** backups of files and the database, kept for **7 days**.
Worst case, data since the last nightly backup (about 24 hours).
Restore is best effort, usually within one business day.
A formal restore arrangement can be agreed in the contract.

full.title: Separation of customer data
items: Each organisation sees only its own data.
A user or API key of one customer cannot read or change another customer’s data.
Staff can be limited to the locations assigned to them.

full.title: Roles and access
items: **Administrator**: organisation, users, subscription and teams.
**Employee**: day-to-day work (issues, tasks, locations), without account or billing administration.
**Worker**: tasks via the field portal, without an email account. A team leader can manage workers and linked phones.
API keys get separate permissions, for example read issues only.
Reports (CSV or print) follow the same permissions as the lists in the app.

full.title: Sign-in
items: Back office: email and password. Passwords are stored hashed. Repeated failed attempts are temporarily blocked.
Self-registration works only after the link in the confirmation email. Unconfirmed sign-ups are deleted after 7 days.
**Sign in with Microsoft** (desktop): only an existing account whose email matches. No automatic new accounts. Email and password still work.
Other software uses a revocable access token with chosen permissions, not the ordinary login.
Workers sign in via Clock Point (name and personal icon, or a PIN or biometrics). No email account.
Reporters use the public QR portal without an account. With optional email confirmation, the issue is created only after the link.

full.title: Security
items: HTTPS, hashed passwords and a revocable API token.
Protection against actions from another website while someone is signed in.
Separation between organisations, plus a log of important actions.
Outbound webhooks are signed, so the receiver can check that the message comes from WinProx.
The API, the public report form and the back-office login limit repeated requests.
QR issues on the public portal stay invisible until an administrator approves them.
Support access is exceptional and read-only by default.
A phone is linked to one worker. An administrator or team leader can release that link. Repeated wrong sign-in stays blocked until release.
Optional PIN or biometrics. Optional GPS check on clock-in.

full.title: Privacy (GDPR)
items: **Customer = controller**; WinProx = **processor**.
Framework: EU GDPR and Belgian law. A data processing agreement and a list of subprocessors are available.

Data stays in the **EU** (hosting and email). When paying, Stripe may also process in the EU or the US. With Sign in with Microsoft the user goes to Microsoft; WinProx receives the email address (and possibly the name) to recognise an existing account.
Account export and self-service deletion of the organisation. Retention periods are fixed.
Optional email confirmation for a QR issue: an unconfirmed draft is deleted automatically, including photos. No user account.
A planned roster is optional. Restoring a previous version is limited to people who may edit the roster, and only for a limited time.

Optional presence reporting to the Belgian social security office (CIAO). The national register number is stored encrypted. The customer enters the enterprise number. Successful submissions are deleted after a limited period. An export without the national register number is available.

full.title: Availability
items: Available 24/7 as an online service (browser and QR portals).
A unit page that is already loaded stays usable briefly without a network and syncs afterwards. Clock-in needs a connection.
On a fixed clock display the code changes, so an old photo of the screen does not stay valid.
Planned maintenance preferably outside office hours, with notice when possible.
A formal availability arrangement can be agreed in the contract on request.

full.title: Clock display (optional)
items: Optional fixed touchscreen on site, linked to a Clock Point. Rented separately with the subscription; no purchase through WinProx required.
Network: **2.4 GHz Wi‑Fi**, **WPA2** and **WPA3-Personal**. Connection to WinProx via **HTTPS** (EU).
Pair with a one-time code in the back office. Unlinking revokes the device.
Without a smartphone: first name and PIN for clock-in, clock-out and **break**. Repeated wrong attempts are temporarily blocked.
CE-marked for professional use; powered via USB-C (5 V).

full.title: Integrations
items: **REST API** with **JSON** responses, on **Corporate** (trial on request). Documentation for integrators is on API & Webhooks.
Including issues, tasks, locations, units, teams, workers, checks, measurements and ESG.
Outbound webhooks on events, signed, with automatic retries. Same plan as the API.
IoT sensors via a separate gateway token (Corporate).
Sign in with Microsoft on the desktop is not a connection for other software.

full.title: Checkmate
items: The same platform and the same separation between organisations, with a smaller set of screens for people who work at customer sites.
**€5** per active worker per month.
Trial: 25 licences for 30 days.

full.title: AI translation
items: Operational texts can be translated on WinProx infrastructure, not via a public AI cloud.
Administrators can correct translations by hand.
Translation supports the work; it does not decide on processes.

api_webhooks.label: API & Webhooks
api_webhooks.tagline: Integrate WinProx with your existing software via APIs and webhooks.
api_webhooks.highlight: WinProx is not a replacement for existing IWMS or ERP systems. Thanks to APIs and webhooks, WinProx works alongside them.
api_webhooks.intro: WinProx is built so other software can use the same data, issues, tasks and unit checks as WinProx itself. Admin and docs live under Settings → API. Desktop Sign in with Microsoft is not an API link: other software uses tokens, not SSO. Leave and TOIL requests have time.absence.* events (no write REST API in this slice).
api_webhooks.footer_right: See also: Features and capabilities · Technical fact sheet

left.title: Why APIs and webhooks?
left.body: With the API and webhooks, WinProx can work with existing software. For example:
items: automatically forward an issue to your IWMS, CMMS or ERP;
forward a unit check (OK/Not OK) to your external facility software;
record a unit measurement (POST /units/{unit}/measurements);
receive a unit check from your external facility software (via external unit ID);
synchronise tasks with an ERP system;
show data in Power BI;
let IoT sensors create issues automatically;
connect to your own software or Microsoft Power Automate.
left.emphasis: Your central system (IWMS, ERP, BI) stays in the lead — WinProx complements it on the shop floor.

rows: Your system asks WinProx for something
WinProx sends a message to your system

left.title: What this is not
items: Not every action is available via the API. Some parts are intentionally read-only or support only specific actions. That keeps integrations safe and manageable.
You manage webhooks in the app, not via the API.
A generic inbound webhook endpoint for arbitrary external systems is not a product feature yet (IoT and Stripe have their own paths).
API & outbound webhooks: Corporate (trial API on request).

right.title: REST API
right.body: The API lets other software safely retrieve data or perform actions inside WinProx. Communication uses standard REST endpoints and JSON.
items: **Access:** personal access token (Bearer). Revocable. Per token you choose permissions (scopes), e.g. read issues only.
**Organisation boundary:** each token belongs to one organisation; you never see another customer’s data.
**Safety:** request rate limit per minute. Optional Idempotency-Key so a repeated request does not create a duplicate action.
**IoT separately:** sensors use a gateway token (Corporate), not the same API token.

rows: Issues, Tasks, Locations, Units, Teams, Workers, Unit checks, Unit measurements

Clock in/out, shifts (API clock-in does not bind a phone); release bound device; manual clock-in (POST /api/v1/time/manual-clock-in, admin source, does not bind a phone); apply minimum break (POST /api/v1/time/work-shifts/{id}/apply-required-break); teams expose required_break_minutes; GPS work visits POST /api/v1/time/work-visits/start (unit_id or location_id) and .../end (time:write); webhooks time.visit.started / time.visit.ended. Planning (GET/PUT /api/v1/time/schedule and shift-types) returns 403 when the roster is off; clock-in stays

right.title: Outbound webhooks
right.body: WinProx sends an HTTP POST to a URL you provide whenever something happens.
items: **Setup:** Settings → API → Webhooks (URL + which events). The secret is shown once — store it safely.
**Proof of origin:** each message has an HMAC signature (verifiable with your secret).
**Reliability:** if delivery fails, WinProx retries (with increasing delay). Deliveries appear in a log.

**Other events include:** issue created / approved / status changed · task created / started / completed · Time (incl. CIAO presence) · GPS · ESG · reservations · test button · unit check recorded. With email confirmation: **issue created** only after the link. time.visit.started / time.visit.ended.
right.emphasis: Example: a worker completes a task. WinProx automatically sends a webhook to your external system (IWMS, CMMS or ERP) so a work order can be updated immediately.

full.title: Ready for integration
full.body: WinProx is designed to work alongside existing systems. Suitable for integration with, among others:
items: IWMS / facility management
CMMS / maintenance systems
ERP
Microsoft Power Automate
Power BI
Custom software
IoT platforms
full.emphasis: Have an existing IT landscape? We are happy to explore how WinProx fits. Contact: info@winprox.app · Documentation: Settings → API → Docs
